text: The Patriots made a significant move along their offensive line this week, signing OL Matt Pryor from the Arizona Cardinals practice squad to bolster protection around quarterback Drake Maye, though that infrastructure took a concurrent blow when guard Greg Van Roten was placed on injured reserve with a thigh injury. Maye himself addressed concerns about his right shoulder Wednesday, insisting the physical condition hasn't affected his throwing ability and instead pointing to the need for better decision-making to reverse the team's 1-2 start—a sentiment that carries weight given New England's alarming offensive output, currently last in the NFL at 9.7 points per game. The 1-2 Patriots head to Buffalo's new Highmark Stadium on Sunday for an AFC East clash against the undefeated 3-0 Bills, where they'll face a Josh Allen team known for its ability to shake off sloppy performances, making this early-season showdown a crucial opportunity for New England to demonstrate whether Maye and the offense can correct course before falling further behind. Off the field, Ann Maye, wife of the Patriots quarterback, volunteered at Family Food Connections and presented a $100,000 donation from the MayeDay Family Foundation to support the food pantry's mission to combat food insecurity in the community.
